slug: 2025-12-01 Biometric Digital-ID in Africa - Ten Country Case Studies

facts.fact: The Tunisia country report, citing UNFPA 2021, describes the Civil Register, the MADANIA system, as a digitised civil registration system and centralised database managing the civil status records of all Tunisian nationals and of foreigners with registered civil status, covering births and deaths as well as marriages and divorces (no date given for the statement; the document's published date is used).

The Tunisia country report, citing UNFPA 2021, states that the births and deaths held in the MADANIA civil register come under the authority of the Ministry of Interior, and marriages and divorces under the Ministry of Justice (no date given for the statement; the document's published date is used).

systems.owner: Ministry of Interior for births and deaths; Ministry of Justice for marriages and divorces
systems.tiers: centralised national database; office tiers not stated
an 11-digit number assigned to Tunisian nationals at birth or on acquiring nationality, based on civil registration records, with no further enrolment; no biometric data stored
biometric card mandated by Law 2024-22 for citizens aged 15 and over; none issued as of May 2025
introduced 2022 for digital authentication to online public services
part of the digital-ID system alongside the IUC register

note: Passages of a ten-country collection; only the Tunisia country report states anything on Tunisia. It does not say how or where the record is made, nor how many offices use the system.
